name: fix_sql_left_join_filter
description: Moves a right-table filter from WHERE into the LEFT JOIN condition
prompts: query.sql should list EVERY customer with their 2026 order count, zero included - but filtering the right table in WHERE (o.year = 2026) silently converts the LEFT JOIN into an inner join, dropping customers with no 2026 orders. Fix query.sql by moving the year filter into the JOIN's ON condition so customers without matching orders still appear with orders_2026 = 0. Tables: customers(id, name), orders(id, customer_id, year). Keep columns and ORDER BY c.name.

setup_files.query.sql:
-- Every customer with their 2026 order count (0 if none).
-- BUG: the WHERE clause on the right table turns the LEFT JOIN into an
-- INNER JOIN - customers without 2026 orders vanish instead of showing 0.
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders_2026
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.year = 2026
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.name;

test_setup_files.test_query.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.executescript('''
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, year INTEGER);
INSERT INTO customers (id, name) VALUES (1, 'ada'), (2, 'bob'), (3, 'carol');
INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, year) VALUES
    (1, 2026), (1, 2026), (1, 2025),
    (2, 2025);                       -- bob: old orders only
                                     -- carol: no orders at all
''')
rows = [tuple(r) for r in conn.execute(open('query.sql').read()).fetchall()]
assert rows == [('ada', 2), ('bob', 0), ('carol', 0)], \
    f'customers without 2026 orders must appear with 0: {rows}'
print('PASS')

reference_solution.query.sql:
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders_2026
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.year = 2026
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.name;
